messages:
maya: Heads-up — we started seeing a cluster-wide jitter in per-GPU latency around 01:05 UTC, looks correlated with a single rack. Noticed a bunch of tenants spiking small-batch requests.
sam: Thanks, Maya. Any host-level signal (nvlink errors / thermal) or is it request-side?
maya: Mostly request-side but NVSM logs show intermittent pci_errs on host-rack-12-03. Metric query I ran: ```sum(rate(gpu_kernel_latency_ms[1m])) by (host) | topk(10)``` — host-rack-12-03 is top.
li: Can we throttle in the scheduler or move noisy tenants off that rack? Which tenants are heavy?
maya: Tenant IDs: t-7523, t-8891 are the biggest culprits (lots of tiny completions, high qps). They’re on shared pool fractional slices.
devon: If we evacuate slices we want to avoid warmup cold-start cost. Option: soft-evict noisy slices to spare nodes + redirect new allocations to dedicated-slice pool for affected tenants.
sam: Agreed. Also consider NIC shaping for the rack to smooth bursts — less disruptive than full evacuation. Dev cost low, but impacts throughput for everyone on that rack.
li: Can we try a temporary routing override: route t-7523/t-8891 to eu2-dedicated-burst for next 30m while we probe? Routing policy change is low-risk and reversible.
maya: I can open a canary: change routing for 10% of their traffic now, 50% in 10m, full in 20m. Watch latency/kv cache miss. Will annotate in the runbook.
ops-bot: @channel Routing override applied for tenant t-7523 -> eu2-dedicated-burst (canary 10%).
devon: Good. Simultaneously, let's flip on host-level packet pacing on rack-12 to reduce NIC queue length. li — can you file the quick NIC patch? Template: ```tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 1000```
li: On it. I'll push to canary hosts first.
sam: Also think about longer-term: these tenants are tiny-batch QPS heavy — recommend a new quota/classification: small-req qps cap + incentivized batching. Could be part of Optimize / pricing conversation.
maya: Agree. Short-term mitigation plan: 1) routing canary to dedicated-burst, 2) host packet pacing, 3) watch NVSM errors. If we see nvlink or thermal, escalate to hardware.
li: ETA for NIC patch rollout to canary hosts: 8 minutes. I'll post progress.
maya: Monitoring dashboards updated to include per-tenant small-batch qps and kvcache hit rate. Link: https://grafana.redwood/gpu-noise/dash
devon: If the canary works, we should automate traffic-sheoarding when queue depth > threshold (avoid manual toggles). Ticketing that now.
ops-bot: @devon Ticket INF-2319 created: "Automate noisy-tenant sharding based on queue depth".
maya: Early canary results: 10% shows a 12% reduction in tail latency on rack-12 hosts, kvcache misses unchanged. nvlink errs still occasional.
sam: Good win. Let's increase to 50% in 5m and keep NIC shaping live.
li: 50% rollout started.
maya: 50% looks stable. I'll keep watch for 30m — if nvlink errs persist escalate to hardware ops.
devon: Cost note for routing to dedicated-burst: expect ~1.6x token-cost for those tenants while on the dedicated pool vs shared cache — flagging for finance.
maya: Noted — I'll add a short aftermath blurb in the incident slack thread with cost delta.
sam: Thanks all. Follow-up actions: li to finish NIC patch rollout to remaining canary hosts; devon to own automation ticket; maya to run postmortem with tenant owners and cost impact. :thumbsup
